exposure: Maternity care provider type (obstetricians, family practice physicians, midwives)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 85,835 women with low-risk pregnancies who gave birth in Manitoba, Canada, between 2004/05 and 2012/13.
finding: Midwifery care for low-risk women was associated with lower odds of C-section, induction, and episiotomy but higher odds of postpartum hemorrhage and shorter hospital stays compared to obstetrical care, while family practice physicians showed decreased odds of assisted vaginal delivery, epidural use, and severe tears but higher odds of augmentation.
mod_finding: Midwifery care was associated with lower odds of cesarean section, induction, and episiotomy, while family practice physicians had decreased odds of assisted vaginal delivery.
